title: Where ZIA reads and writes disagree: an index of round-trip hazards

prose.text: Some ZIA fields read back differently from how they were written, and the detail for each lives in its own subject. This page only points to them.

prose.label: Sandbox default rule order.
prose.text: The default Sandbox rule reads as order 127 and what the API does with that value is open: [[zia.sandbox.rules]].

prose.label: Location time zone and country.
prose.text: The API recently changed how the Netherlands time zone is spelled and which form a write accepts is open: [[zia.locations.country-timezone]].

prose.label: Rule description whitespace.
prose.text: The provider suppresses description diffs and whether the server rewrites whitespace is open: [[zia.api.url-filtering-wire]].

prose.label: User authentication methods.
prose.text: The Terraform user resource accepts a narrower set than the API: [[zia.terraform.multi-step-writes]].

checks.do: Whether a drift or rejection on a rule, location or user is one of these known round-trip cases before treating it as a tenant change.
Whether a read-back write fails on server-assigned fields such as id, creationTime or modifiedTime. The legacy note that they are ignored is unverified.
For a DUPLICATE_ITEM on a default rule, do not create or manage the default rule through Terraform or the API, and do not import default rules.
For a rejection on an SSL Inspection default rule, check its read-only fields before writing; which fields the API rejects is open.

server-fields-ignored.title: Whether server-assigned fields can be sent back on write
server-fields-ignored.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Server-assigned fields like id, creationTime and modifiedTime are echoed on read and ignored on write; stripping them is fine but not required.' No captured ZIA source states this for these fields.

read-only-fields-on-write.title: Which read-only fields the API rejects on write
read-only-fields-on-write.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Some resources have read-only fields the API rejects on write, such as the ZIA SSL Inspection default_rule and predefined rules.' The captured SSL Inspection sources say only that default and predefined rules cannot be deleted and predefined ones can be imported (zia.api.ssl-inspection-wire:predefined-not-destroyable).
